facts.raw_span: a three-week history of a tender, slow-growing left axillary lump
a low-grade fever (37.5–38°C) for one week
hypertension—treated with lacidipine, lisinopril, and hydrochlorothiazide
a laparoscopic Roux-en-Y gastric bypass performed two years earlier
lost 112 kg (BMI from 64.6 to 28 kg/m2)
smoked 30 cigarettes daily
took vitamin (A, D, E, B complex), calcium, cholecalciferol, and iron supplements
a tender, non-mobile, 3 × 4 cm lymph node in the left axilla

laboratory studies—including a complete blood count, ESR, liver and renal panels, autoantibodies (ANA, RF), complement levels, inflammatory markers, thyroid function, and serologies for a broad spectrum of viral and parasitic pathogens—were all normal or negative
a thoracoabdominal CT scan was unremarkable except for the axillary lymphadenopathy
a biopsy of the axillary node revealed coagulative necrosis with frequent karyorrhexis and a lymphoplasmacytoid infiltrate
an investigation for mycobacteria was negative

concepts.why: The patient's presentation with a tender axillary lymph node, low-grade fever, and biopsy findings of coagulative necrosis with lymphoplasmacytoid infiltrate are consistent with cat-scratch disease.
The patient's symptoms and biopsy findings, including coagulative necrosis and lymphoplasmacytoid infiltrate, are also consistent with Kikuchi-Fujimoto disease.
The patient's presentation with a tender axillary lymph node and biopsy findings of coagulative necrosis with lymphoplasmacytoid infiltrate could also suggest Rosai-Dorfman disease.
The patient's symptoms and biopsy findings, including coagulative necrosis and lymphoplasmacytoid infiltrate, could also be consistent with Castleman disease.
The patient's presentation with a tender axillary lymph node, low-grade fever, and normal laboratory studies could also suggest sarcoidosis.
The patient's symptoms and biopsy findings, including coagulative necrosis and lymphoplasmacytoid infiltrate, could also be consistent with lymphoma.
Although the investigation for mycobacteria was negative, the patient's presentation with a tender axillary lymph node and low-grade fever could still suggest tuberculous lymphadenitis.
The patient's symptoms, including a tender axillary lymph node and low-grade fever, could also be consistent with brucellosis.
The patient's presentation with a tender axillary lymph node and low-grade fever could also suggest toxoplasmosis.
The patient's symptoms and biopsy findings, including coagulative necrosis and lymphoplasmacytoid infiltrate, could also be consistent with histiocytosis.

rationales.F01: The presence of a tender, slow-growing left axillary lump is more typical of Kikuchi-Fujimoto disease.
rationales.F02: Low-grade fever is a non-specific symptom that can be seen in various conditions, including Kikuchi-Fujimoto disease.
rationales.F08: The presence of a tender, non-mobile lymph node in the left axilla is more typical of Kikuchi-Fujimoto disease.
rationales.F11: The biopsy findings of coagulative necrosis with frequent karyorrhexis and a lymphoplasmacytoid infiltrate are highly suggestive of Kikuchi-Fujimoto disease.
rationales.F12: The negative investigation for mycobacteria rules out Tuberculous lymphadenitis.
